newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean Jan-June trade surplus falls to $531 mln.
newsitem.headline: Chilean Jan-June trade surplus falls to $531 mln.

text.p: Chile reported a trade surplus of $531 million in the first six months of the year, down from $611 million in the same period last year, said the Central Bank in its monthly report.
In June, the surplus rose to $40 million from $6 million in the same month last year mainly as a result of a steep increase in the value of copper exports.
"The value of copper sales abroad in June rose 21 percent on the same month last year as a result, in large part, of the rise in copper prices," said the report.
Main exports other than copper, which include wood pulp and fishmeal, rose four percent in June after tumbling in previous months, said the report.
"This year these exports have fallen 10 percent in value so far this year, which reflects fundamentally the drop in value of fishmeal and fresh fruit exports," it said.
Fishmeal exports have been hit by temporary bans on mackerel fishing, while figures for fruit exports do not yet fully reflect prices paid for fruit abroad, it said.
Non-traditional exports, which include salmon and wine, rose 12 percent in June on the same month last year.
